title: test all runs its 2282 tests one at a time on a 16-core Mac: run them in parallel where GNU parallel is installed, and the tests that need the machine to themselves on their own
body:
## Problem

`bin/devbin test all` runs `bats tests/unit` with no `--jobs` (bin/.devbin/cmd/test:64-68, at 9fedef14), so the suite's 2282 tests run one after another. That took 40.6 min on this Mac, which has 16 cores (hv's run of 9fedef14, seal 20261008-1740, 2282 of 2282 ok), and 39.5 min on CI's 2-CPU Ubuntu runner (run 37818416586). The median test takes 0.72 s on CI. A cut runs the suite in its dry run and again in its gates, and every landing runs it once.

Raised by hv on 2026-10-08 from dc's profile of the suite, which vc checked against the code and CI's own timings.

## Measured (dc, 2026-10-08, at 9fedef14)

- bats 1.14.0 runs tests in parallel with `--jobs N` through GNU parallel, which it calls with `--keep-order`, so the TAP stream keeps its order. `test bats` already forwards bats's own flags (bin/.devbin/cmd/test:40).
- GNU parallel is not installed on this Mac. CI's Ubuntu image ships it: runner-images' Ubuntu2404-Readme.md at ubuntu24/20260927.320 lists parallel 20231122+ds-1.
- A read-only audit of all 52 files found nothing that blocks parallel runs. No test writes into the checkout, uses `setup_file` state, depends on another test's state, or uses a fixed path outside its own mktemp directory. After 11 files ran in a scratch clone, `git status --porcelain --ignored` there was empty.
- About ten tests have wall-clock margins that CPU contention could eat: heartbeat.bats:85, 105 and 115; clean.bats:524 and 536; fullcycle.bats:994; releasecut.bats:1704, 1783 and 1827. Two load the machine themselves: the full-tree lint at contract.bats:1050, which runs up to eight shellchecks, and prettier at vendoredmd.bats:115.
- Not yet measured: a real parallel run.

## Fix

When GNU parallel is installed, `test all` runs the suite with `bats --jobs N`. Tests that need the machine to themselves are tagged (eg `# bats test_tags=serial`) and run on their own after the rest. Without GNU parallel, it runs as it does today, and the run's header says so. N is printed in the header and can be set. Its default is the builder's measured choice for this Mac, and it leaves room for another estate's runs on the same machine. The run still ends in one verdict over every test, and the seal under tmp/test/ carries it as today. GNU parallel goes onto this Mac on hv's go of 2026-10-08.

## Done when

1. With GNU parallel installed, `bin/devbin test all` runs the parallel lane and then the serial lane. Its seal gives one verdict over all of them: every test runs once, none is missing, and failures are named as today.
2. Without GNU parallel, or with N set to 1, the suite runs serially as today, and the header says why.
3. Each test that failed under `--jobs` in the builder's runs is either in the serial lane or fixed, and the Resolution gives the reason. Two consecutive full suites under `--jobs` on this Mac are green.
4. CI's Ubuntu job runs the suite under `--jobs` and is green on the pushed head before the cut.
5. The Resolution gives the wall time before and after, on this Mac and on CI. The `test` help page says how the lanes work and how to set N.

## Resolution

Landed at e29f9f07 on a green full suite (vc's, 2295 of 2295 ok, 0 not ok, .errors empty, seal 20261008-2007).

1. `bin/devbin test all`, and `test bats` handed nothing for bats, run the whole suite through `bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/bats-lanes`, a new script beside `shell-gate` that `cmd/test` runs through `run_gate`, so the run is sealed as before. Where GNU parallel is installed it runs two lanes:
   - every test not tagged `serial`, N at a time, under `bats --jobs N --filter-tags '!serial' tests/unit`;
   - then the tests tagged `serial` (`# bats test_tags=serial` on the line before a test, or `# bats file_tags=serial` before a file's first), one at a time, under `bats --jobs 1 --filter-tags serial`, given only the files that carry the tag, since bats preprocesses every file it is handed before it runs one (about 9 s for the whole suite here).
2. One seal, one verdict. The run's exit is non-zero when either lane fails, and when the lanes did not run every test exactly once between them. What ran is counted with the seal's own counter (`count_for shell`) and held against an untagged `bats --count tests/unit`, taken beside the parallel lane rather than before it. The last line says how many ran in each lane, and on a shortfall names it: `lanes: 3 test(s) ran in parallel and 0 serially, 3 in all, but bats counts 4 in tests/unit: the lanes did not run every test exactly once`. An empty serial lane is never run, because bats 1.12 (CI's) and 1.14 (this Mac's) differ there: 1.12 prints `1..0` and exits 0, and 1.14 exits 1.
3. N is on the run's first line, with the GNU parallel found and the CPU count: `lanes: two. First 8 tests at a time under GNU parallel 20260922 (16 CPUs here; DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS sets the number), then the tests tagged serial, one at a time`. The default is half the CPUs and never fewer than two: 8 here, and CI's runner prints its own. `DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS` sets it; a value that is not a whole number of at least 1 is refused, naming it.
4. Without GNU parallel, or with `DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS=1`, the run is `bats tests/unit` as before, and the first line says why: `lanes: one, serial, because GNU parallel is not installed: there is no parallel on PATH (brew install parallel, or apt-get install parallel)`, `... because the parallel on PATH, <path>, is not GNU parallel` (a moreutils `parallel`), or `... because DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS is 1`. The probe asks for the program bats itself will run, `BATS_PARALLEL_BINARY_NAME` or `parallel`.
5. A run handed paths or bats flags is a targeted run, unchanged: bats gets exactly what it was handed, in one lane, and its own `--jobs` works there.
6. `cpu_count` moves into lib/helpers as the one home for the CPU probe (nproc, then getconf, then 4); the lint gate, which wrote it inline, now calls it.
7. CI provisions GNU parallel on both legs: `parallel` on the Ubuntu apt line and on the macOS brew line.
8. The `test` help page has a section on the lanes: what runs in each, N and `DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS`, the fallback, the targeted run, and how and why to tag a test serial. `help test bats` points at it. intent/llm/MODULES.md registers the new script.

The serial lane holds one file, heartbeat.bats, whole, by `# bats file_tags=serial`. Five of its nine arms, as 0191 leaves it, rest on a fraction of a second of scheduling, which tests running beside them could eat:
- three need a beat inside a 1 s gate;
- the fractional interval's arm reads its beats in windows of a second or less;
- the chatty gate must see no beat, and a writer stalled for about 0.4 s fires one. Its whole-second ancestor flaked twice on the macOS runner with nothing beside it (2026-09-15 and 09-16, by its own comment).

The file is tagged for how it is built, not for a failure, and its header says why. The tag is the file's rather than each arm's because a test tag did not follow an arm that changed in another patch: v1 tagged four arms on the 0191 head it was built on (542711c1), and 0191's final head made the exit-status arm a fifth, asserting that a beat fired inside its 1 s gate. With the file tag, an arm added to the file runs serially too. The four arms that assert no timing come along; the whole file took 12 s on its own.

Every other arm the read-only audit named passed under `bats --jobs 8` over main, with seconds of margin to spare, while another node's two targeted runs held the box at load 27 to 41, and stays in the parallel lane:
- clean.bats:524 and 536;
- fullcycle.bats:994;
- releasecut.bats:1704, 1783 and 1827;
- the two that load the machine: contract.bats's full-tree lint and vendoredmd.bats's prettier.

heartbeat.bats's three, at main's whole-second beats, passed there too; 0191 has since made its beats a fraction of a second, and the file runs serially.

Done when 3, the tests that failed under `--jobs`: none. Two runs each had one failure, and `--jobs` caused neither:
- the measurement over main, below, failed install.bats:812, because of its checkout's one-letter name (found in passing, below);
- the first two-lane suite failed dispatch.bats:2914 on 0190's own first draft of cmd/test, which hid from that test's raw-argv scan the split arguments it counts. v1.1 fixed it before the two green suites below.

Done when 5, the wall time:

- This Mac, before: 40.6 min, hv's serial run of 9fedef14 (seal 20261008-1740, 2282 of 2282).
- This Mac, after: 10.5 min (627.0 s) under BSD tools and 9.8 min (586.7 s) with GNU tools first on PATH, the two-lane suites below, each 2294 of 2294.
- CI's Ubuntu job, before, one lane: 42.1 min for the whole job (run 37818416586 on 9fedef14, green; its Run tests step 39.7 min).
- CI's Ubuntu job, after, two lanes: 43.5 min for the whole job (run 37842539047 on 73fd0fd3, green; its Run tests step 43.1 min). The steps are not like for like, since lint moved from the gates step into the tests between those runs, so the whole job is the comparison: on CI's 2-CPU runner the lanes bought no time. Read from GitHub's job and step times (2026-10-14, again 2026-10-26); added after the close on hv's ruling of 2026-10-26, with no issue filed.

The arms, in testhandler.bats, all carrying 0190 in their titles. Two are the handler's: handed nothing, or a wrapper flag alone, it hands the gate `bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/bats-lanes tests/unit`. Nine run the lane runner for real over a four-test fixture suite with one test tagged serial, its test lines written as printf arguments because bats reads any line of a .bats file that starts `@test` or `# bats` as the file's own:

- two lanes, N at a time and then the serial test, each test once, the serial test in the serial lane only;
- a failing test in either lane fails the run;
- a serial lane that comes back empty, from a bats that answers `1..0` to the serial filter, fails the run on the count;
- without GNU parallel (`BATS_PARALLEL_BINARY_NAME` naming no program), with a `parallel` that is not GNU's, and with `DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS=1`: one lane, every test, and the reason on the first line;
- `DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS` of 0, x, 2.5 and -3 refused, naming the value, before any test runs;
- the default, from a fake `nproc` of 6 and of 3: 3 jobs and 2;
- no test tagged serial: no serial lane, and the run says so.

Evidence, in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-dc/0190/runs/, the seals in runs/seals/.

- Red on main 40883674 first, the build's testhandler.bats copied in, under BSD tools and with GNU tools first on PATH (red-40883674-{bsd,gnu}-20261008-191345.log): all 11 arms red, the same under both. The two handler arms fail on the argv, `bats tests/unit`; the nine lane arms on the missing script.
- testhandler.bats green on the build under bats 1.14 with BSD tools, with GNU tools first on PATH, and under bats 1.12.0, CI's pin, fetched into scratch (archive sha256 e36b0204...).
- The default, measured: raw `bats --jobs 8 tests/unit` over main 40883674, before any of 0190, took 611.5 s for its 2282 tests, against 40.6 min for the serial run of 9fedef14, also 2282 tests: about four times faster (measure.txt, jobs8-bsd-40883674-20261008-190218.tap). Eight is half of this Mac's 16 CPUs, which leaves the other half to another project's runs. N above 8 was not measured.
- The full suites, `bin/devbin test all` in two lanes, one heavy run on the box at a time (suites.txt):
  - v1 at 911f6ecf, BSD tools: 637.7 s, red, 2293 of 2294 (dispatch.bats:2914, above); the lanes counted 2290 and 4, 2294, each once.
  - v1.1 at 56740cf1, BSD tools: 627.0 s, green, 2294 of 2294: 2290 in parallel, then 4 serially, each once. Another project's publishing shared the box for its first minutes.
  - v1.1 at 56740cf1, GNU tools first on PATH: 586.7 s, green, 2294 of 2294, the same split.
  - Both green suites ran on 0191's 542711c1, with v1's four test tags in heartbeat.bats. vc's suite of the landing tree runs the final whole.
- The final rebase, onto 0191 v1.1 at 21f523d9, met one conflict, in heartbeat.bats, resolved with the file tag above; the other five commits replayed unchanged. heartbeat.bats then ran alone, 9 of 9 in 12 s, on a trial rebase onto 0191's 2b719467 (fin190-20261008-1956.bats.out). v1.1 changed no byte of heartbeat.bats, lib/runlog, lib/helpers or tests/lib, so nothing more ran.
- critic-shell reviewed v1. All of its findings are folded except one recommendation:
  - test-check, two criticals: two lane arms read N only from the run's first line. With `--jobs` deleted from the script they stayed green, because bats runs files under GNU parallel with `--keep-order`, so a two-job stream reads exactly like a one-job one. The arms now read what each lane hands bats, from a `bats` on PATH that records its argv:
    - the parallel lane gets `--jobs 2 --filter-tags !serial tests/unit`;
    - the serial lane gets `--jobs 1 --filter-tags serial tests/unit/b.bats`;
    - the defaults are `--jobs 3` and `--jobs 2`.
  - test-check, a warning: `lanes_run` let an outer run's `DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS` reach the arms, which help's own example sets. It now clears that, `BATS_PARALLEL_BINARY_NAME` and `BATS_NUMBER_OF_PARALLEL_JOBS`.
  - The code review found no critical and no warning, and three recommendations. Two are folded:
    - each lane's exit status is named on the last line when it is not 0, since a lane can fail with no `not ok` line, and the seal's log tail shows that line;
    - `cpu_count` says when it takes 4. The default-jobs arm drives that with `nproc` and `getconf` both failing.
  - The third is not taken: one helper for the make-a-scratch-directory-and-trap-its-removal idiom, which `shell-gate`, `bats-lanes` and the release core's `open_scratch` each write. vc read the sites and settled it with no issue: each inlines the same two lines, and lib/ has no general helper they bypass.
  - heartbeat.bats's file tag came after that review, at the final rebase, and vc read it.
- The patch: `git diff 21f523d9..2231259e`, 10 files, 516 lines in and 9 out, sha256 3aa75fd3d817e6241b0d64357665573d4aa2c6ae0e4c2e42585d27def44469b0 (drafts/0190-2231259e.patch). Applied to a fresh clone at 21f523d9 it goes on clean, and every file it touches then has 2231259e's bytes. A bundle of the six commits, which needs 21f523d9, sits beside it.

Declared limits:

- The default leaves half the machine to another project's runs; it does not see them. On a machine already loaded, `DEVBIN_TEST_JOBS` is the lever.
- bats's own scheduler polls for a free slot once a second (lib/bats-core/semaphore.bash), and on macOS, which has no flock, its slot lock is shlock's, which also waits in whole seconds. Neither is devbin's to change.
- Found in passing, not 0190's: install.bats:812 sets HOME to the checkout's path less its last character, which for a checkout whose directory name is one character long is the checkout's parent, and the test then fails. A scratch clone named `m` met it.
